meta.title: GSiS v0.9.2 · ownership and data flow

views.label: Staff journey
views.note: Browser interactions enter app-specific gateways; backend owners authorize changes.

views.label: Source ownership
views.note: Separate owners exchange signed minimal projections rather than sharing write access.

views.label: Notification delivery
views.note: Durable intents govern delivery; optional infrastructure does not become business authority.

cards.title: Nine apps · six backend owners
items: Contacts manages staff identities and application access. Calendar owns school dates, parity and events. Deploy owns planning/publication; Layout shares its backend and physical room register.
Roster owns baseline, suspended and relief timetable state. Venues owns room bookings and facilities permissions. LORD, OVERLORD and STARLORD share one booking/device backend.

cards.title: Identity and source exchanges
items: Private staff apps retain Google sign-in/session checks. STARLORD keeps its read-only display model and separate outer access policy. Venues also supports verified Access JWTs; its backend resolves active Contacts identity and facilities grants.

Roster reads Contacts authority over a signed bridge and published Deploy quota/catalogue through read-only workbook access; its gateway gets Calendar date context. LORD refreshes signed Contacts/Deploy manifests. Venues reads signed Contacts, Deploy/Layout, Calendar and Roster projections.

cards.title: Venues admission and timetable precedence
items: A signed Roster begin creates a durable Venues fence before occupancy-changing timetable writes. Unrelated absence and audit work can continue. Complete marks the source stale; sync activates only when captured revisions and fence tokens still match.

Server validation checks current permissions, date coverage, room rules, pending holds, closures and effective timetable occupancy. Booking/transfer effects, audit, receipt and notification intent commit together in the Venues workbook. No cross-service atomicity is claimed.

cards.title: Stores, delivery and maintenance
items: Each Apps Script project owns its mutable records and locking. Roster retains Drive JSON; Venues uses atomic Sheets batch updates and immutable Drive occupancy pieces. Browser caches accelerate reads but never authorize a write.

The Roster Worker claims durable intents; optional Queue messages only wake it. Optional R2/D1 serve documented Roster media, snapshots and webhook jobs. LORD and Venues dispatch their own notifications. Uncertain provider acceptance requires review.

This source map is a companion to README.md, the deployment authority. It describes repository contracts, not a live infrastructure audit. See the editable Draw.io pages and evidence JSON for exact source ownership.

cards.title: Local source evidence
items: Source identity: local GSiS_v0.9_Correction_Source_History.bundle. No hosted upstream is asserted. The pinned revision, source ranges and file hashes are retained in architecture-evidence.json and architecture-source.json; architecture-text.md is the text alternative.

Archify cannot verify local-bundle origins. Its passing gates cover the rendered artifact and browser behavior; repository provenance is checked separately against local Git objects. README.md remains the only deployment guide.
